purpose: Test whether a small reconstructed spectral correction captures useful finite-precision stabilization after charging its replay cost.
representation: Keep the initial actual kernel columns; add at most four learned vectors and count all additional retained and transient storage.
selection: Largest Ritz values; identify relative duplicates at sqrt(machine epsilon), then verify physical independence using the reconstructed M-Gram matrix.
scalar_lanczos_convention: For q_i=z_i/sqrt(rho_i), use negative off-diagonals; preserve first-pass alpha, beta, rho and operation order during replay.
replay: Twenty sequential operator products, with every preconditioner application and vector accumulation counted. No change of recurrence or reorthogonalization during replay.
small_matrices: Normalize independent reconstructed modes in the M metric; recompute T=U^T A U from actual reconstructed images.
initial_correction: x <- x + U T^{-1} U^T r; verify its true residual and include a correction-only old-preconditioner control.
methods: coarse correction followed by old preconditioner
coarse correction followed by balanced Ritz-LMP
strong_controls: Unpreconditioned CG, compact RP and Gaussian-power factors using the same retained-vector allowance; use each LMP representation actual retained state to determine the control rank.
balanced_storage: A boundary-vector implementation is allowed only after validating the Lanczos residual relation against actual A-images. Full U/AU storage is a separately counted reference, not a free substitute.
checks: true original relative residual at most 1e-8
retained and transient storage including candidate vectors
decision: Advance only if continuation savings repay replay and survive storage-matched strong controls. No prefix/rank/threshold sweep after a negative result.
novelty_boundary: Spectral-LMP, Ritz-LMP, same-solve recycling and two-pass Lanczos reconstruction are established. This experiment establishes neither novelty nor success of the project by itself.
